plain_claim: For every environment `env`, rejected-instance predicate `R : Inst → Bool` and rewrite `ρ`: if every instance `ρ` targets satisfies `R`, then for every verdict relation `verified` sound for the law-free semantics `compiledDen env`, verification transfers (`TransferSound`) through `capRejectRewritable R` — which rejects every program containing a syntactic call of an instance in `R` and captures every other program unchanged — to the compiled program rewritten by `ρ` (`capRejectRewritable_compiledDen_transferSound`); and the capture is incomplete: `capRejectRewritable cloneToCopy.targets` rejects `probe 0 5` although in `envSafeTriv` every compiled run of the rewritten probe is already a run of the unrewritten probe (`capRejectRewritable_incomplete`).

hypotheses.name: hR : ∀ i, ρ.targets i = true → R i = true
hypotheses.purpose: every call site that `ρ` can rewrite must be rejected by `capRejectRewritable R` (applies to `capRejectRewritable_compiledDen_transferSound`)
hypotheses.witness_class: `R = fun _ => false`, `envSafeLog`, `cloneToCopy`, and the exact verifier of `compiledDen envSafeLog` on `probe 0 5`

hypotheses.name: hV : VerifierSound (compiledDen env) verified
hypotheses.purpose: accepted verdicts must hold of the pre-rewrite law-free semantics `compiledDen env` (applies to `capRejectRewritable_compiledDen_transferSound`)
hypotheses.witness_class: the unsound verifier `fun _ _ => True` accepting every specification on the empty program `[]` in `envSafeTriv`

nonvacuity_witness: `nonvacuity_capRejectRewritable`: `R = cloneToCopy.targets`, the exact verifier of `compiledDen envSafeLog`, and an accepted program `[.call 1 1 0]` calling untargeted instance `1`.
non_claims: The verifier semantics in `hV` is the law-free semantics `compiledDen env` (every call runs its impl, no relies check). For a verifier sound for `capDirectDen` instead, `TransferSound` does not hold in general: for the exact verifier `fun q spec => CaptureBridge.Sat (capDirectDen envUnsafeLog .before q) spec`, `capRejectRewritable cloneToCopy.targets` accepts `probe 1 5` and fails to transfer the UB-tolerant specification `fun r => r.2 = .ub []` (`cex_capRejectRewritable_not_transferSound_for_capDirect`). Note also the `CaptureBridge` parameter roles: `semS` is instantiated to the post-rewrite compiled program `fun p => compiledDen env (ρ.apply p)` and `semV` to the pre-rewrite `compiledDen env`.
`callsSome` is a purely syntactic check over `p`, so `capRejectRewritable` also rejects programs whose targeted calls are unreachable (such as `[.ub, .call 0 1 0]`) or dead (`deadCall`).

The hypothesis `hR` covers a single rewrite `ρ`; extending the `env`-universal sufficiency theorem `capRejectRewritable_compiledDen_transferSound` from `ρ.apply` to a rewrite sequence `applySeq ρs` would take `R` covering every rewrite in `ρs` (or `(firstMatch ρs).targets`) (not stated as a separate theorem here; for a fixed `env` where `ρs` acts as an observational identity, such as `envSafeTriv`, `TransferSound` can hold without `R` covering `ρs`).
Incompleteness is witnessed by one concrete program in `envSafeTriv`; how much coverage a real verifier loses by rejecting rewritable calls is not examined.

tier_justification: Because every replacement in `Rewrite` is call-free inline code `prim f` that no later `Rewrite` matches, `applySeq ρs` collapses algebraically to the single rewrite `(firstMatch ρs).apply` (`applySeq_eq_firstMatch`), reducing sequence refinement directly to `refinesPP_capDirect_apply_of_lawOnReached`.
plain_claim: For every environment `env`, relies position `pos`, list of rewrites `ρs`, program `p` and store `σ`: if for every rewrite `ρ ∈ ρs` its law holds at every call of a targeted instance that the law-free execution of `p` from `σ` reaches (`LawOnReached env ρ p σ`), then the compiled program obtained by applying the rewrites of `ρs` in order (`applySeq ρs p`) refines, prefix-preservingly, the direct capture of `p` from `σ`.

hypotheses.name: hlaw : ∀ ρ ∈ ρs, LawOnReached env ρ p σ
hypotheses.purpose: every rewrite in `ρs` must agree with the impl at the reached calls of `p` that it may replace
hypotheses.witness_class: a sequence `[cloneToCopy]` of exactly one rewrite, `envSafeLog`, initial store `σ0`, relies point `before`, and `probe 0 5`

nonvacuity_witness: `nonvacuity_applySeq`: `envSafeTriv`, `[cloneToCopy, cloneToCopy1]` on a program calling both instance `0` and instance `1` from `σ0`.
non_claims: Within this call-free `prim` model, `applySeq ρs p = (firstMatch ρs).apply p` (`applySeq_eq_firstMatch`), so no sequence of `LawOnReached`-satisfying rewrites can interact to break refinement. That non-interaction relies on two strong restrictions: (1) per-program refinement `RefinesPP` itself is NOT closed under sequential composition when an earlier rewrite refines `p` without obeying `LawOnReached`, because changing an unobserved intermediate return value can change the argument reaching a later rewrite's call site (`cex_refining_rewrites_seq_not_refining`); and (2) rewrites whose replacements contain trait calls (such as redirecting one method to another) are not modelled — if an earlier rewrite can introduce a call to an instance unreached in `p`, `LawOnReached` on the original program `p` no longer suffices (not proved here).

Composing unsafe-trait rewrites without `LawOnReached` (under `TargetsUnsafe` and `ReplIsContract`) and laws relating two instances (such as cross-trait consistency between `Eq` and `Hash`) are not covered by this theorem.

tier_justification: Folklore made precise: call-free rewrites with pairwise-disjoint targets compose conjunctively over all contexts without shadowing, whereas overlapping targets allow an earlier rewrite to shadow a later invalid rewrite.
plain_claim: For every environment `env`, relies position `pos` and list of rewrites `ρs`: if no two rewrites in `ρs` target a common instance (`ρs.Pairwise TargetsDisjoint`), then `applySeq ρs` refines, prefix-preservingly, the direct capture on every program and every initial store iff every rewrite `ρ ∈ ρs` satisfies `ContextSafeAt env pos ρ i v` at every instance `i` it targets and every argument `v`.

hypotheses.name: hdisj : ρs.Pairwise TargetsDisjoint
hypotheses.purpose: with overlapping targets an earlier rewrite replaces the calls a later rewrite would match, so the shadowed later rewrite need not satisfy `ContextSafeAt`
hypotheses.witness_class: the sequence `[cloneToCopy, succRewrite]` of at most two (specifically, two) rewrites targeting instance 0 in `envSafeTriv` at relies point `before`, quantified over all programs and stores

nonvacuity_witness: `nonvacuity_applySeq`: `[cloneToCopy, cloneToCopy1]` in `envSafeTriv` at relies point `before` (pairwise disjoint targets; `ContextSafeAt` holds everywhere).
non_claims: Under the stronger `LawOnReached` hypothesis (`LawAt` rather than `ContextSafeAt`), per-program sufficiency holds without `hdisj` (`refinesPP_capDirect_applySeq_of_lawOnReached`); sufficiency of the `ContextSafeAt` conjunction without `hdisj` is not proved here. Without `hdisj`, the left-to-right (necessity) direction fails for `[cloneToCopy, succRewrite]` in `envSafeTriv` at relies point `before`, where the earlier `cloneToCopy` satisfies `LawOnTargets` and shadows `succRewrite`, which fails `ContextSafeAt` at instance `0` and argument `0` (`cex_overlapping_rewrites_conjunction_not_necessary`).

Because replacements are call-free `prim` statements and targets are pairwise disjoint, the rewrites in `ρs` do not create or consume matches for one another; pass-ordering sensitivity in real compilers (where one pass creates or enables matches for another) and multi-instance laws are not modelled.

tier_justification: Monotonicity of nondeterministic over-approximation under inclusion of per-step choices (Back & von Wright 1998; `Refine_Monadic`, Lammich 2012), restated for `applySeq` and `CoveredBy`.
plain_claim: For every environment `env`, lists of rewrites `ρs` and `ρs'`, program `p` and store `σ`: if every replacement of every rewrite `ρ ∈ ρs'` is the replacement of some rewrite in `ρs` at the same instance (`∀ ρ ∈ ρs', CoveredBy ρs ρ`), then every behaviour from `σ` of the compiled program `applySeq ρs' p` belongs to `capRel env ρs p σ`.

hypotheses.name: hcov : ∀ ρ ∈ ρs', CoveredBy ρs ρ
hypotheses.purpose: every replacement that `applySeq ρs'` may substitute at an instance must appear among `capRel env ρs`'s choices at that instance
hypotheses.witness_class: empty capture list `ρs = []`, `ρs' = [cloneToCopy]`, `envSafeLog`, initial store `σ0`, and `probe 0 5`

nonvacuity_witness: `nonvacuity_coveredBy`: `ρs' = [succRewrite]` covered by `ρs = [cloneToCopy, succRewrite]` on `probe 0 5` from `σ0` in `envSafeLog`.
non_claims: Both `capRel` and `compiled` are law-free semantics that ignore `env.safety` and `env.contract` and perform no relies-point UB checks (`capRel_unsafe_ignores_contract_example`). Verifying a specification of `capRel` transfers to `compiled` and neither establishes `Sat (capDirect env pos p σ) spec` nor rules out unsafe-trait UB in other passes or unsafe consumers.

`capRel env ρs` is an over-approximation, not weakest, for whole-program sequences `applySeq ρs'`: even for a singleton list `[cloneToCopy]`, `applySeq [cloneToCopy]` rewrites all matching sites uniformly, whereas `capRel` admits mixed per-site runs (`cex_capRel_not_weakest_for_all_or_nothing`).

Every rewrite of `ρs'` in the statement is applied at all sites via `applySeq`; per-site partial application of a multi-rewrite list is not stated (per-site partial application of a single rewrite is characterized in `mem_capRel_iff_exists_applyAt`). Separately, `relCalls_append` shows that at each call `(i, v)`, `relCalls env (ρs₁ ++ ρs₂) i v` is the list concatenation (`++`, preserving order and duplicates) of `relCalls env ρs₁ i v` with `(relCalls env ρs₂ i v).tail`.
